digest.lede: The week's biggest story is the US government treating AI model releases like weapons exports — Anthropic's Mythos cleared for limited use, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 restricted before launch, and Asian labs moving fast to fill the gap. Meanwhile, Google DeepMind is hemorrhaging senior researchers to OpenAI, and OpenAI is raiding Apple hardware leadership. The candidate pool implications are real. Full intel below.

talent_trends.takeaway: Google DeepMind lost Noam Shazeer to OpenAI — when a $2B acqui-hire walks, the talent war is escalating beyond normal retention tools.
talent_trends.context: Noam Shazeer, co-author of the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' transformer paper and one of the most consequential researchers in AI, left Google DeepMind for OpenAI last week. Google had paid over $2 billion to acqui-hire Shazeer and part of his Character.ai team. His departure is the second high-profile researcher Google DeepMind lost in a single week. For talent partners at AI labs and their investors, this is a signal that even historically unprecedented retention packages are not holding at the frontier — and that OpenAI's gravitational pull around AGI timelines is now the dominant recruiting pitch.
talent_trends.source_title: Google takes the hit in AI's talent war

talent_trends.takeaway: Apple's VP of Vision Pro is joining OpenAI's hardware team — senior hardware leaders are now a target segment for AI lab recruiting.
talent_trends.context: Paul Meade, the Apple VP responsible for Vision Pro, is reportedly leaving for OpenAI's hardware team. This is a meaningful signal: OpenAI is building out a serious physical hardware organization and is looking to Apple's executive bench for that talent. For recruiters advising AI-native companies, Apple's hardware leadership layer is now a live sourcing pool — especially anyone with experience in spatial computing, optics, or consumer device manufacturing. Watch for more Apple hardware departures as the OpenAI device story develops.
